name.description: The name under the face, 40 characters at most.

slot.description: The rival slot the face rode in, 0 first. The slots are filled by `faces` at their slot numbers and then by `rivals` in order, so a face sits ahead of the handles, as it did on the player's screen.

image.description: The face: a 256×256 JPEG, 64 KB at most, cropped to the middle of the photo. Readers refuse a bigger one.

face.description: One of the player's own faces, as it rode in a run: which rival slot, the name under it, and the picture.

log.description: The whole run as the only input the game takes. Comma-separated `<dtick>.<k>.<a>` entries: dtick is 60 Hz ticks since the previous entry; k 1 holds (a 1) or lets go (a 0) of the trigger; k 4 gives up; k 5 sets the tank's controls to a = (throttle + 1) * 3 + (turn + 1), each -1, 0 or 1. Only inputs the sim accepted are logged. Example: `96.5.7,30.1.1,18.1.0`.

seed.description: The mazes: `arcade` (the same for everyone), or a UTC date `YYYY-MM-DD` for that day's. Each has its own board.

faces.description: The player's own photo faces that rode in rival tanks, included on purpose (the game asks, off by default) so a replay anywhere shows them; each photo is a public blob in the player's repo. Looks only, like `rivals`: a face takes its slot ahead of the handles, the rivals' play is the sim's, and a verifier ignores this field entirely. Six at most.

level.description: Advisory: the maze the run ended on, 1 to 18, three a world.

ticks.description: Advisory: 60 Hz ticks from the first count to the end of the run.

rivals.description: Handles whose faces the rival tanks wore (people the player follows). Looks only: the rivals' play is the sim's and doesn't depend on this.

difficulty.description: The difficulty the run was played at; absent means normal. A verifier must replay at it, and each has its own board.

simVersion.description: Which rules produced this log. A verifier must replay under the matching version or refuse the run.

main.description: One Sky Tanks run, published by the player into their own repo. The record stores every input rather than trusting a score: the sim is deterministic, so replaying the log on the same seed reproduces the run exactly. Owning the record is the identity proof, and replaying it is the score proof; score, ticks, level and the rest are advisory and never trusted by a board.
